cohort: 688 healthy women with singleton pregnancies from three hospitals in Chengdu, China, recruited between 2013 and 2014
finding: Sleep disturbances during pregnancy, particularly poor sleep quality and short sleep duration, were associated with an increased risk of both cesarean delivery and preterm birth.
mod_finding: Women with poor sleep quality during all three trimesters had increased odds of cesarean delivery (OR ranging from 1.82 to 5.19).
birth_weight: Neonatal weight recorded, but specific details not provided
